text: For years, AI has been good at specific tasks, like translating languages or recognising faces. This is called narrow AI. Now, researchers are working towards general AI, often called AGI, which would understand and learn any task a human can. AGI could bring major benefits, such as faster medical research and smarter education tools. However, it also carries risks, including job losses and safety concerns if systems are poorly controlled. Experts disagree about the timeline. Some believe AGI could arrive within ten to twenty years, while others think it is much further away. Either way, careful planning and clear rules will be essential.
